title: Inside the model: build, test and measure a MiniGPT
language: English; Chinese translation only when explicitly requested

transformer_modules.purpose: See how the original 2017 Transformer connects input and output sequences.
transformer_modules.math: A representation is a vector at each position; N x repeats blocks.
transformer_modules.difference: Our decoder-only model has no encoder and no cross-attention. Its blocks use Pre-LN; the original figure shows Add & Norm after sublayers.

transformer_modules.figure_box: Left encoder stack and its Multi-Head Attention
transformer_modules.purpose: Read the given source sequence and produce representations for the decoder to consult.
transformer_modules.math: Encoder self-attention gets Q,K,V from the source sequence; decoder cross-attention uses its output for K,V.
transformer_modules.difference: The original encoder can attend across the supplied source sequence. This causal decoder-only MiniGPT does not implement that encoder or its unmasked source-attention branch.

transformer_modules.purpose: Turn discrete character IDs into trainable vectors.
transformer_modules.difference: The local input uses 96 character symbols, not a commercial tokenizer. IDs come from data.py.

transformer_modules.purpose: Provide the position of each token.
transformer_modules.difference: The original paper uses sinusoidal positions; this model learns a position table.

transformer_modules.purpose: Supply known characters while the target is the following character.
transformer_modules.difference: The supplied character windows express next-token shifting without adding a special translation start token.
Our causal switch is used only for the controlled failure demo; normal attention stays causal.

transformer_modules.figure_box: Multi-Head Attention inside the masked decoder sublayer
transformer_modules.purpose: Learn several mixtures of the same input features.
transformer_modules.difference: A Python list comprehension is explicit teaching code; it does not imply automatic simultaneous kernel execution.

transformer_modules.figure_box: Middle decoder Multi-Head Attention with arrows from encoder
transformer_modules.purpose: Read encoder information using decoder queries in translation.
transformer_modules.math: Q from decoder; K,V from encoder.
transformer_modules.difference: Omitted in this decoder-only model. Do not call the middle decoder box another copy of its masked self-attention.

transformer_modules.purpose: Add a computed change to the representation and normalize features.
transformer_modules.difference: Pre-LN is an intentional difference from the original Post-LN diagram. These operations help training; they do not guarantee gradients can never vanish or explode.

transformer_modules.purpose: Apply the same nonlinear feature transform separately at each position.
transformer_modules.difference: This MiniGPT uses GELU. The 2017 paper uses ReLU. FFN itself does not mix token positions.

transformer_modules.purpose: Repeat blocks to build deeper representations.
transformer_modules.difference: L=2 here. Heads are registered with ModuleList; blocks with Sequential so the optimizer can find their parameters.
forward returns raw logits; the added final norm is part of this MiniGPT implementation.

transformer_modules.purpose: Convert scores to probabilities when sampling the next character.
transformer_modules.difference: Generation applies Softmax for sampling. F.cross_entropy handles logits directly in training; do not apply Softmax twice.

transformer_modules.purpose: Relate repeated matrix work to measured CPU/CUDA performance.
transformer_modules.math: tokens/s=steps*B*T/time; one score matrix has B*h*T*T elements.
transformer_modules.difference: The device comparison measures a fixed training interval. It excludes I/O, transfer, evaluation, generation and plotting.

concepts.title: Model, parameters and training
concepts.brief: A model is a numerical rule with adjustable numbers called parameters. Training changes those numbers using examples. Calling an API or editing a prompt does not itself update them.
concepts.example: For y = w*x, w is a parameter. Changing x changes this answer; changing w changes the rule used for future answers.

concepts.title: Scalars, vectors, matrices and tensor shapes
concepts.brief: A scalar is one number. A vector is a list of numbers. A matrix has rows and columns. A tensor is an array with one or more axes. [B,T,d] means B sequences, T positions and d features at each position.
concepts.example: [2,8,128] stores two sequences, each with eight token positions, each position holding 128 numbers. These numbers are not temperatures.

concepts.title: Token IDs, embeddings and positions
concepts.brief: A token is a unit of text. Here it is one character. Its integer ID selects a row from a trainable embedding table; a position vector adds where that character occurs.
concepts.example: The same M has the same token embedding at positions 1 and 17, but different position embeddings. Use encode('M12 ') to see the real IDs.

concepts.title: Dot products, scaling and Softmax
concepts.brief: A dot product multiplies matching vector entries and adds them. Matrix multiplication repeats row-column dot products; transpose swaps axes. We divide scores by the square root of the head width. Softmax uses exp(score), meaning e raised to that score, then divides by the sum to produce nonnegative weights adding to one.
concepts.example: q=(1,0) and k=(1,1) have dot product 1. Softmax of three equal scores gives 1/3 to each. The weighted sum combines Value vectors.

terms.Dot products, scaling and Softmax: A dot product multiplies matching vector entries and adds them. Matrix multiplication repeats row-column dot products; transpose swaps axes. We divide scores by the square root of the head width. Softmax uses exp(score), meaning e raised to that score, then divides by the sum to produce nonnegative weights adding to one.

concepts.title: Causality and the mask
concepts.brief: At position t the model predicts the next token using input positions up to t. A causal mask prevents later inputs from leaking into that prediction. It acts on scores before Softmax.
concepts.example: If inputs begin M12, the output at M predicts 1. That output can read M but cannot read the target 1 from the next input position.

terms.Causality and the mask: At position t the model predicts the next token using input positions up to t. A causal mask prevents later inputs from leaking into that prediction. It acts on scores before Softmax.

concepts.title: Linear layers, GELU, residuals and LayerNorm
concepts.brief: A Linear layer applies learned weights and a bias. GELU is a nonlinear transformation. A residual adds a module's change to its input. LayerNorm normalizes each position's feature vector and applies a learned scale and shift.

concepts.title: Logits, probability, loss, gradients and updates
concepts.brief: Logits are scores for the possible next characters. Softmax turns scores into probabilities. Cross-entropy penalizes low probability on the correct next character. A gradient describes how loss changes with a parameter; the optimizer uses gradients to update parameters.
concepts.example: For the correct character, p=0.1 gives -ln(p) about 2.30 and p=0.7 gives about 0.36. ln is the natural logarithm; use a calculator, with no calculus required here. backward() computes gradients; optimizer.step() changes parameters. Cross-entropy takes logits directly.

terms.Logits, probability, loss, gradients and: Logits are scores for the possible next characters. Softmax turns scores into probabilities. Cross-entropy penalizes low probability on the correct next character. A gradient describes how loss changes with a parameter; the optimizer uses gradients to update parameters.

concepts.title: Warm-up, timing, throughput and device synchronization
concepts.brief: Warm-up prepares the computation before timing. Throughput is work divided by measured time. CUDA operations can finish after the CPU launches them, so synchronize at both timing boundaries.
concepts.example: 200 steps * 16 sequences * 64 positions = 204800 training positions. Divide that count by the actual measured seconds. This is not generated characters per second.

concepts.title: Validation, sampling and memory statistics
concepts.brief: Validation uses data that did not update parameters. Sampling picks a next character from probabilities, then repeats. Process RSS measures resident process memory; PyTorch allocated CUDA memory measures allocations tracked by PyTorch on the GPU.
